title: Chalk Detective
objective: Describe the observable properties of chalk and choose its safe use or handling.

items.prompt: Maxine gently tests objects with an adult. Which material is flexible?
items.explanation: A rubber band bends and returns to shape, so it is flexible. Stone, glass, and metal resist bending or can break.

items.prompt: Milo wipes water with cloth, a rubber duck, and a glass jar. Which absorbs water?
items.explanation: Cotton cloth has fibers that soak up water. Rubber, glass, and a wooden ruler do not absorb the spill as well.

items.prompt: Milo gently presses four objects. Which material is hard?
items.explanation: A stone stays firm and resists bending, showing hardness. Foil, rubber, and sponge are more flexible or soft.

items.prompt: Maxine writes with chalk and sees a dusty mark. Which property does the chalk show?
items.explanation: Chalk is soft enough to leave a powdery mark, so soft and dusty describes the observation.

items.prompt: Before studying chalk, which action is safe?

options.text: Look at it and touch it gently

items.explanation: Looking and gentle touching are enough for a safe observation. Throwing, soaking, or tasting chalk is unsafe.
